name: Lettuce Seeds
descriptions: Small pale seeds packaged for quick germination; sow in shallow soil and keep moist to grow crisp lettuce.
Crunchy and mild when eaten raw — a tiny, refreshing nibble that supplies a small bit of energy.
effects: You pop a few seeds into your mouth; a faint, refreshing crunch and a mild, vegetal flavor.
A few seeds chewed provide a small filling sensation and a slight energy lift.

name: Carrot Seeds
descriptions: Tiny dark seeds ideal for direct sowing into loose, deep soil to encourage straight roots.
Bitter and nutty eaten raw in small amounts — a modest snack that offers a little energy.
effects: Sow in deep, loose soil and thin seedlings to allow carrots to develop over several weeks.
A few seeds chewed provide a small filling sensation and a slight energy lift.

name: Cactus Seeds
descriptions: Hard, tiny seeds intended for arid conditions; germinate slowly and prefer sandy, well-draining soil.
Very dry and bland if eaten raw — only a slight, short-lived energy boost from the sugars they contain.
effects: Plant in sandy soil and avoid overwatering; grown cactus will tolerate dry conditions and store water.
Eating a few seeds gives a minimal energy pick-me-up but little fullness.

name: Tomato Seeds
descriptions: Small flat seeds removed from ripe fruit; sow in warm soil and transplant seedlings to a sunny spot.
Slightly tangy when chewed; eating some seeds gives a pleasant small energy boost similar to snacking on the fruit's seeds.
effects: Start indoors or direct sow; transplanted seedlings develop into fruiting tomato plants in warm weather.
A mouthful of seeds provides a small, tangy energy boost and light fullness.

name: Strawberry Seeds
descriptions: Tiny seeds typically surface-mounted on the fruit; plant in fertile soil with good drainage and regular moisture.
Sweet and familiar — the same tiny seeds found on strawberries give a small, pleasant energy boost when eaten.
effects: Plant in nutrient-rich soil and keep evenly moist; mature plants will produce sweet strawberries.
Eating a pinch of seeds is sweet and satisfying, offering a noticeable small energy and hydration boost.

name: rose seed
descriptions: A small, hard seed from a cultivated rose. Can be planted to grow a decorative rose bush or chewed for a faintly floral taste.
Plantable in a small pot or garden bed; requires regular watering and sunlight to sprout.
effects: Chewing releases a subtle floral aroma and lightly sweet flavor.
Plantable: germinates into a rose bush after proper stratification and care.

name: sunflower seed
descriptions: A shelled sunflower seed — crunchy and oily, commonly eaten as a snack or pressed for oil. Also planted to grow tall sunflowers.
Easy to plant in a sunny spot; seeds sprout into large flowering stalks that attract pollinators.
effects: A crunchy, satisfying snack that provides a small but noticeable energy boost.
Plantable: grows into a sunflower that can later yield many more seeds.

name: mint seed
descriptions: Tiny mint seeds that can be planted to grow fragrant mint plants. Chewing a few seeds produces a quick minty burst.
Mint prefers partial sun and moist soil; it spreads readily once established.
effects: A quick refreshing minty flavor that slightly soothes and refreshes.
Plantable: grows into a fast-spreading mint plant useful for culinary and herbal uses.

name: basil seed
descriptions: Small basil seeds that can be planted to grow aromatic basil plants. Crushed seeds have a faint herbal scent and can be consumed in small amounts.
Best grown in warm, well-drained soil with plenty of sunlight; great for culinary use once mature.
effects: A mild herbal taste that complements food; provides a modest fullness and gentle energy lift.
Plantable: grows into basil plants whose leaves can be harvested for cooking.
